key_concepts: Earthquakes release energy in the form of seismic waves
The focus or hypocenter is the point inside the crust where seismic waves are released
The epicenter is the surface point directly above the focus
Magnitude is the total energy released by an earthquake
Intensity describes shaking and damage in a particular area
Magnitude is measured with the Richter scale and expressed in numbers
Intensity is rated with the Modified Mercalli scale in Roman numerals from I to XII
Active faults produce shallow earthquakes because rock displacement occurs
